claims.text: Longitude 131 has views direct to Uluru and across the desert to Kata Tjuta.

findings.quote: With views direct to Uluru and across the desert to Kata Tjuta

claims.text: The lodge sits on privately owned land surrounded by Katiti Aboriginal Land and the dual World Heritage listed Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park.

findings.quote: Longitude 131° is situated on 23,800 square metres of privately owned land and is surrounded by Katiti Aboriginal Land and the dual World Heritage listed Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park.

claims.text: Guests stay in tented pavilions among the dunes, with floor-to-ceiling glass framing the desert light.

findings.quote: Nested among ancient dunes, Longitude 131° is a gathering of sixteen tented pavilions
Floor-to-ceiling glass frames the ever-changing light of the desert

claims.text: Longitude 131 first opened in 2002, with safari-style tents gathered around a central Dune House designed by Australian architect Philip Cox.

findings.quote: Longitude 131° first opened to global acclaim in 2002, with its gathering of safari-style guest tents around a central Dune House the creation of leading Australian architect Philip Cox.

claims.text: The lodge's sustainable design includes renewable energies and the ability to be dismantled and removed entirely.

findings.quote: the lodge’s sustainable design includes renewable energies and the ability to be dismantled and removed entirely

claims.text: Spa Kinara uses irmangka-irmangka, also known as Scented Emu Bush, a bush medicine used by Aboriginal healers, in many treatments.

findings.quote: A powerful bush medicine used by Aboriginal ngangkari or healers, irmangka-irmangka is also known as Scented Emu Bush and is used in many treatments at Spa Kinara.

claims.text: Signature experiences include a guided sunrise expedition to Kata Tjuta and Walpa Gorge.

findings.quote: Embark on a guided sunrise expedition to Kata Tjuta and Walpa Gorge

claims.text: Artist Bruce Munro's Field of Light installation is one of the signature experiences.

findings.quote: Artist Bruce Munro’s Field of Light installation of 50,000 bud-like stems

claims.text: Scenic helicopter flights lift off from the lodge's helipad, at additional charge.

findings.quote: Longitude 131° works with premium local operators to offer these special adventures. Additional charges apply, view rates here.
lifting off from the lodge’s helipad on a scenic helicopter flight

claims.text: Dining combines premium produce from around Australia with bush ingredients.

findings.quote: The finest premium produce is delivered to the Red Centre and combined with bush ingredients to offer guests a unique taste of Australia.

claims.text: The in-tent bar is included in the stay.

findings.quote: A stay at Longitude 131° is generously all-inclusive, even down to the in-tent bar.

claims.text: Each luxury tent offers views to Uluru from the end of the bed.

findings.quote: fifteen luxury tents at Longitude 131° each offer views to Uluru – from the end of the bed!

claims.text: The Dune Top has a help-yourself bar, outdoor lounges and a plunge spa with views to both Uluru and Kata Tjuta.

findings.quote: the Dune Top is an intimate space comprising a help-yourself bar, outdoor lounges and plunge spa with views to both World Heritage-listed natural icons Uluru and Kata Tjuta.

claims.text: Signature experiences are included in the tariff and run on a shared basis with fellow guests at scheduled times.

findings.quote: These experiences are included in the tariff and are provided on an intimate shared basis with fellow guests at scheduled times.

claims.text: Spa Kinara is inspired by the design of the wiltja, the traditional shelter of the local Anangu people.

findings.quote: Spa Kinara is inspired by the clever design of the _wiltja,_ the traditional shelter of the region’s Indigenous Anangu people.

claims.text: The lodge hosts artists-in-residence visits with Ernabella Arts, where guests can watch Anangu artists paint with views of Uluru and Kata Tjuta.

findings.quote: the 2026 artists-in-residence program with the First Nations Anangu artists from Ernabella Arts
welcomes Ernabella artists to the lodge to paint with sweeping views of Uluru and Kata Tjuta. During these visits, guests are invited to observe the creative process

claims.text: Longitude 131 welcomes children ten years and over.

findings.quote: Longitude 131° welcomes children ten years and over.

claims.text: The gateway is Ayers Rock Airport, three hours by air from most Australian capital cities.

findings.quote: The main port, Ayers Rock Airport is three hours’ travel by air from most Australian capital cities.

claims.text: Conde Nast Traveler notes the pool is a bit petite.

findings.quote: "The pool is a bit petite, but it’s a small price to pay for the overall experience."
